focus: The OpenCode and Pi session readers, projection shapes, redaction and the 160-character preview cut
noveltyJustification: All 8 findings are new: the reader failure envelope, the non-object argument coercion and the measured 295-versus-160 preview offset were not previously recorded in this packet.
keyQuestions: What does each runtime's prepare text tell the sender about keeping details out of the note, and does it over-promise what a fresh session can recover through the History Lookup?
What claim text and History Lookup offer does the receiver read on OpenCode versus Pi, and what makes a receiver leave a claim unverified instead of running the lookup?
How do the OpenCode and Pi session readers feed the History Lookup, including their tool-call argument shapes and secret redaction, and what does each fail to recover?
Does model and effort carry on relaunch for each runtime, and where can it silently degrade or be dropped?

Which known limits (OpenCode store without a directory column, AI_SESSION_CHILD leaking into test sandboxes, the 160-character preview cut, a double nudge from two hooks) cause a hop to fail, and what concrete fix addresses each?

graphEvents.label: What do the OpenCode and Pi readers fail to recover?
Non-object tool-call arguments become an empty object
An OpenCode store without a directory column cannot prove the session folder
A tool-result pairing defect is reported as store_unreadable
The browse preview cuts 135 characters before the live side word

label: Tool-call arguments that are not a plain object are silently replaced with an empty object, so a runtime storing arguments as a JSON string yields a turn that renders as the tool name plus {} and loses the path, command or figure inside it.

An OpenCode store without a directory column cannot prove which folder a session ran in and the reader does not fail closed, so the claim mint treats acceptance as folder proof and the same-checkout invariant is unenforced on exactly those stores.

One orphaned, duplicated or mismatched tool result fails the whole projection and is reported as store_unreadable, the code that tells receivers the store is missing or unreadable, so a single bad pairing costs the session history and misdiagnoses the cause.

Pi finds a historical session only by exact project directory plus exact header id plus matching header cwd and refuses ambiguity, which makes the note's cwd load-bearing: a note whose cwd differs from the directory Pi keyed the session under gets no lookup at all.

The lookup CLI reads through the projected path, which returns items only, so hook-injected messages never reach a receiver; a detail that arrived as an injected block rather than a user or assistant turn is outside the lookup's reach.

Redaction runs once before projection over text, thinking and tool-call arguments, with credential-shaped keys replaced whole and other strings scrubbed, so no route reaches a raw entry while a secret under a neutral key such as command survives unless a value pattern matches.

The 160-character browse preview hides the live case's side word: previewFor slices to 160 characters while the side word sits at character 295 of the 425-character sender prompt, so a receiver running exactly the offered browse would not see it in the preview.

Search previews are centered on the matched token while browse previews take the leading slice, and the offer leads with browse, the one operation that cannot center on a value the receiver does not already know.

direction: Redaction drops tool-call secrets in a shape-dependent way
reason: Object arguments are key-checked and every string is scrubbed; the shape hazard is that non-object arguments are dropped before redaction matters.

direction: The Pi reader enumerates the store and can pick the wrong session
reason: It filters by exact id and refuses two candidates as session_ambiguous.
